text.p: Computer memory card maker Centennial Technologies Inc on Thursday restated its earnings to show losses for the nine months ended March 31 and for the past three fiscal years instead of profits, after completing a financial review.
The action reflects previously reported instances of alleged executive mismanagement.
The company Thursday reported for the three month period ended March 31 a net loss of $0.36 per share versus a restated loss of $0.08 a share the year before.
In the nine month period in 1997, it recorded a restated loss of $1.30 per share against a restated loss of $0.26 a share.

The company said its sales figures were previously inflated, allegedly due to actions taken by its former chief executive, Emanuel Pinez, who has been charged by the Securities and Exchange Commission with insider trading.
Court records show that the inflation was achieved by various means, including shipping empty PC card housings, and billing customers for non-existent product, Centennial said.
As a result of the alleged mismanagement, Centennial's stock was delisted in March, its chief financial officer was fired, and several class-actions suits have been filed against the firm.
Pinez, the former founder and chief executive, has denied, through his lawyer, any wrongdoing.

Centennial said its restated fiscal year 1996 losses were $0.31 per share, with restated 1995 and 1994 losses at $0.63 and $0.19 per share, respectively. The fiscal year ended on June 30 in each year.
The company said total assets at at June 30, 1996 were $41.1 million.

Centennial said cumulative adjustments to previously reported results of operations through December 31, 1996 consist of sales adjustments totaling $22.6 million, inventory adjustments totaling $7.7 million, and write-offs of investments and advances to several companies totaling $15.8 million.

Centennial said it expects to file its March 31, 1997 Form 10-K report to the Securities and Exchange Commission by the end of the month, which the company expects will provide the first substantive step towards the relisting of its common stock on an organized exchange.
